translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel the son of Bethuel.
Hear this, you elders, and listen, all who live in the land. Has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
For what the worm left, the locust ate; what the locust left, the grub ate; and what the grub left, the blight ate.
Wake up, you who are drunk with your wine, and weep. Lament, all you who drink wine until you are drunk, for delight and gladness have been taken from your mouth.
For a nation has come up against my land, strong and without number. Their teeth are lions' teeth, and their back teeth are those of lions' cubs.
It has made my vineyard a ruin and my fig tree a wreck. It has searched it out completely and thrown it down, and it has stripped its branches white.
Lament to me like a bride dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
Offering and sacrifice have been taken away from the house of the Lord. Mourn, you priests who serve at the altar.
For the plains have become desolate. Let the land mourn, for the wheat has been ruined, the wine has dried up, and the oil has run low.
The farmers have withered. Lament, you farmlands, for the wheat and the barley, for the harvest has perished from the fields.
The vine has withered and the fig tree has dwindled. The pomegranate, the palm, the apple and every tree of the field have withered, for they have put to shame the joy of the sons of men.

Put on sackcloth and beat your breasts, you priests. Lament, you who serve at the altar. Go in and sleep in sackcloth, you servants of God, for offering and sacrifice have ceased from the house of your God.
Sanctify a fast, proclaim a healing. Gather the elders and all who live in the land into the house of the Lord our God, and cry out to the Lord together.
Woe is me, woe is me, woe is me for that day! For the day of the Lord is near, and it will come like ruin upon ruin.
Before your eyes food has been cut off, and delight and joy from the house of your God.
The heifers [?] leapt [?] at their mangers. The storehouses are ruined, the winepresses are torn down, for the wheat has withered.
What shall we store up for ourselves? The herds [?] of cattle wept, for they had no pasture, and the flocks of sheep were destroyed.
To you, O Lord, I will cry out, for fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness, and flame has blazed up against all the trees of the field.
The beasts of the field also looked up to you, for the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Proclaim it on my holy mountain, and let all who live in the land gather, for the day of the Lord has come, for it is near:

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like the dawn spread over the mountains comes a people numerous and strong. There has never been anything like it from the beginning, and there will be nothing like it after it, through the years from generation to generation.
Before it is a consuming fire, and behind it a flame blazes up. The land before it is like a paradise of delight, and behind it is a plain of ruin. Nothing will escape it.
Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they pursue like horsemen.
They will leap on the mountaintops with a sound like chariots, and like the sound of a flame of fire that devours reeds, and like a great and strong people drawn up for battle.
Before his face the peoples will be crushed. Every face will be like a pot in the heat,
and they will run like warriors, and climb the wall like fighting men. Each of them will go his own way, and they will not turn aside from their paths.
No one will separate from his brother or his neighbour. They will march weighed down with their weapons, and fall by their own arrows, yet they will not be destroyed.
They will throw themselves upon the city and run along the walls. They will climb onto the houses and come in through the windows like thieves.
Before his face the earth will be thrown into confusion [?], and the heavens will shake. The sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will hide their light.

And the Lord will raise his voice before his army, because his camp is very great, because the work of his words is mighty, because the day of the Lord is great. It is great and fearfully plain to see, and who then will be able to stand against it?
Now the Lord your God says: Turn to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning.
Tear your hearts and not your clothes, and turn to the Lord your God. He is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and full of mercy, and he relents from doing harm.
Who knows whether he will turn and relent, and leave a blessing behind him: a sacrifice and an offering for the Lord our God?
Blow the trumpet in Zion. Make a holy fast. Call people to worship.
Gather the people. Make the assembly holy. Choose the elders, and gather the nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber, and the bride out of her bridal room.

Let the priests who serve the Lord weep between the step and the altar, and let them say: Spare your people, O Lord, and do not let your inheritance become an object of scorn, so that the nations will not rule over them, and so that the nations will not say, 'Where is their God?'
Then the Lord was jealous for his land and spared his people.
The Lord answered his people and said to them: I am sending you wheat, wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied with them. I will no longer make you an object of scorn among the nations.

I will drive the northerner far away from you and banish him into a dry land. I will drive his front into the eastern sea and his rear into the western sea. His stench will rise, and his foul smell will rise, because he has done great things.
Do not be afraid, O land. Be glad and rejoice, because the Lord has done great things.
Do not be afraid, you animals of the field, because the pastures of the wilderness have turned green, the trees have borne their fruit, and the fig tree and the vine have yielded their full strength.
Children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in the Lord your God, because he has given you food in righteousness. He will send you rain, the early rain and the late rain, as he did before.
The threshing floors will be filled with wheat, and the presses will overflow with wine and oil.
And I will repay you for the years that the locust, the fly, the caterpillar and the worm ate: my great army, which I sent among you.
And you will eat and be full, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders among you, and my people will never be put to shame again.
And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides me. And my people will never be put to shame again.

And after this it will happen, says the Lord God, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will see revelations, and your young men will see visions.
And in those days I will pour out my Spirit even on my male servants and on my female servants,
and I will give signs in the heavens and wonders on the earth: blood and fire and a cloud of smoke.
The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and appointed day of the Lord comes.

And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, because on my holy mountain Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who are rescued, as the Lord has said, and among those near ones whom our Lord calls.
Look, in those days and at that time, when I bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will judge them on behalf of my people and Israel, my inheritance, whom they scattered among the Gentiles, because they divided up my land.
And they cast lots for my people. They gave boys to prostitutes and sold girls for wine, and they drank.
And what are you to me [?], Tyre and Sidon? Are you paying me back for something, or are you holding a grudge against me? Quickly and soon I will bring your payback down on your own heads.
Because you took my silver and my gold, and you carried my choicest and best things into your temples.
And you sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel to the sons of the Greeks, to remove them far from their own borders.
Look, I will rouse them from the place where you sold them, and I will bring your payback down on your own heads.
And I will give your sons and your daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them to distant nations, for the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the Gentiles: prepare for holy war. Rouse the warriors. Come and go up, all you men of war,
and beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak man boast, 'I am strong.'
Gather together and come, all you nations round about, and gather there. Let the meek man become a fighter [?].
Rise up, all you nations, and go up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations round about.
Send in the sickles, because the harvest has come. Go in and tread, because the winepress is full and the vats are overflowing, because their wickedness has grown great.
They cried out loudly in the valley of judgment, because the day of the Lord is near in the valley of judgment.
The sun and the moon will be darkened, and the stars will hide their light;
But the Lord will cry out from Zion and utter his voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will be shaken. But the Lord will spare his people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwell in Zion, my holy mountain. And Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer pass through it.

And on that day the mountains will pour out sweetness, and the hills will flow with milk, and waters will flow in all the streams of Judah. A spring will come out from the house of the Lord and will water the valley of the rushes.
Egypt will become a ruin, and Idumea will be laid waste into a bare plain, because of the wrongs done to the sons of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
But Judea will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
And I will demand an account for their blood, and I will not hold them guiltless, and the Lord will dwell in Zion.
